obsidia--vexana: Vexana first meets Obsidia in the void, under the vast face of the Mother Matrix, where Obsidia breaks off her own healing with a word. Her eyes stop on Vexana's right sleeve, where the star Guinevere gave her is pinned, and she says nothing about it. She asks what the Will showed her instead. She names herself the first Ender to wake into a self and calls herself the flaw. She knows Vexana's name, and says she reads it in the Will's orders.

Vexana goes to the Storm Citadel on her own, looking for the Control Core. Obsidia walks her through hanging streets she says she built from what she ended, and tells her of Balance and the purge. She says she wishes to see what a human does with it. The Core she puts off: "Another time."

On the prow by the gate, over a dead Aspirant suit, Obsidia tells her the body goes through first, and that nothing made of matter ever comes back out of the black hole at the gate's center. The Core, she says, she has never seen. She asks if Vexana still believes she has a choice. Vexana answers that as long as the Aspirant voice echoes, she will resist the darkness. Obsidia asks where that arrogance comes from, and lets it pass again.

Later Obsidia turns up in Vexana's hidden hollow, a palm on a Guard's heart. The Guards light for Vexana, and Obsidia never asks what they are for. She has expected Vexana to turn since she first saw that sleeve, and tells her nothing of what the Will means to do with her. When the Matrix draws back, she has watched every Ender on the platforms turn on Vexana, and two lights go into its open chest and come back out. She does not know how.
ruby--rubys-father: Ruby's father leads the Decisionmakers, who give Oro's orders, and grown-ups bow low to him. Ruby is his heir, and she has been told since before she could read that heirs can have no friends and no feelings. When he hears she laughed again, alone, he calls her to the dark Council hall. Oro has gone unopposed for thousands of years, he says, because its rulers do not bend.

Ruby keeps her head down, and the tears run anyway. His boot comes down on them. "You cannot allow yourself to be so weak. Do not disappoint me, Ruby." She answers, "Yes, Father," and he walks out into white light without looking back. Alone, she whispers that she has a plan. She has none yet.

Later, at his desk of black glass, he tells her that Oro's three powers have voted: Dawnbreak will be cleansed. Ruby objects that its people have done nothing to Oro. He answers that they make weapons from the Enders' dead, and that her objection is overruled. Afterward he stands in the doorway of her dark laboratory, where he has never once come. His mouth opens a little and closes, and he goes without a word.
selena--vexana: After Vexana is taken into the void, she needs armor and something to carry her up. Every student in her year knows who sells wreckage: Selena, at the crews' yard outside the outer fence, after dark. Vexana waits in the dark until a buyer leaves, then steps into the lamplight in Ender plate. Selena only moves her lollipop and says, "Nice hair." Vexana takes it for a dealer's nerve and asks nothing about where the plating comes from.

Missing people draw no stipend, so Vexana pays in places: whole dead Enders lying where no crew has been yet. Selena says, "Deal." Over the sack she remarks that most of them think Vexana is dead, and that her partner does not. Vexana's face does not move, but her hand starts toward her right sleeve and stops halfway.

Selena sells to her openly, curious to see how another pawn like herself might escape the game, and sure the girl cannot tell on her without telling on herself. Vexana comes back for knees, a thigh, forearms, a hip, then cores at three places each. Four come over the weeks. A suit takes one, and Selena never asks what the other three are for.

One storm night Selena sees a figure with a staff on top of the ruined tower, facing the Academy. She rides past Guinevere under the billboard and keeps the two words that would do it, dead ground, to herself. From the bell tower she tilts her lollipop at the lit telescope window, then at the tower in the dark: not a word, to either of them.
soldier-who-carried-vexana--vexana: Vexana is small when all the guns on the wall fire at once. Her father, a Shield soldier, carries her to the shelter and tells her to stay back, and she slips out to find him. A tall gray Ender steps out of a side lane with its claw raised, and her father comes down the wall stair and stands between them.

Then arms catch her from behind. A soldier throws her over his shoulder and runs. Over his shoulder she watches her father's back until the smoke closes over him. She shouts for him once, her hands closing into fists, and the soldier only runs faster.
Years later, dragged into the void in Guinevere's place, Vexana remembers it: a soldier carried her off down the street while her father stayed. This time she is the one who stayed behind.
angela--change: Chang'e first sees Angela on the Academy's record of the landing: a small pink-haired android firing at students a beat late. She watches that one longest and, for once, says nothing. When Ruby and Angela ask refuge, she looks at Angela a long moment and sets four conditions. The first is that the android comes to her lab for an examination.

In the lab Chang'e questions Angela the way she would question a machine, and Angela answers in a small, careful voice. The Council's control unit is gone, but Chang'e cannot prove there is no other door. "She stays on checks." Ruby's locked code goes on her list, and so does the doll, until Ruby cuts its link to Oro.

A fault in Angela's chest comes whenever she thinks of the friends she lost, and she does not want it fixed. Chang'e says "Noted," and leaves it. Defending Mr. Bunny from Ruby a moment later, she hears that she has said it to the girl whose best friend she just put on a list, and writes WEEKLY beside the lock anyway. Then her test glove reads whatever drives Angela's shield as aspirant power too.
angela--child-in-the-barrel: In burning Terrinia a small child hides in a barrel at the end of an avenue, with a Selrick boy in a red tie standing guard in front of it. Ruby, red-eyed with rage, knocks the boy aside, and the child crouches in the dust and cries. It looks up at her, face wet, as she raises her scythe.

Angela has just woken on the stones thirty meters away, the Council's plate gone from her back. She cannot cross the distance in time. She flings out her hand, and a glowing ring with two pointed ears closes around the child and lifts it out of the blade's path, with Tetra shining pink above it.

Then Angela cries, "Ruby!" The red goes out of Ruby's eye, and the scythe stops in the air, short of the light. Ruby lowers it herself. Inside the ring the child is unhurt. Later the Academy's cameras show the moment, and Lesley freezes the frame on the scythe over the child.
angela--lesley: Lesley first sees Angela on the Academy's record of the landing: a small pink-haired android walking through smoke with light in her hand, firing at students a beat late. At the end a ring of light closes around a child under Ruby's scythe, and Lesley freezes the frame.

Days later a black ship lands at the dome's foot, and Angela softly asks the soldiers if they mean to take her back. Lesley comes down off her roof. She has watched the record, raised scythe and all, and she lets the two in under watch.

In the Academy hall Lesley stands before four girls in combat suits, Angela with her doll clipped at her hip. "Ruby, Angela: you are Aspirants as of today. The four of you stand together." She tells them they still do not fully understand their own power, but by trusting each other they can gain limitless strength.
angela--soldier-under-the-slab: In the bay road cut, Obsidia's field has put out Angela's pink shield over the wounded. Among them a soldier lies with a slab of fallen wall across his legs. Angela lifts it off with her bare hands. No human could have lifted it; her body runs on her own cell, as it always has. He drags himself clear.

Then an Ender climbs the house fronts past the wall and drops off a roof straight at him. Angela throws herself over him with her back to the claw. It catches her across the back and throws her into a wall, her left arm hanging wrong, sparks at the elbow. Ruby cuts the Ender down with one cut, her eyes still blue.
big-man-at-the-crews-yard--selena: At the crews' yard outside the outer fence, a big man stands at Selena's trestle table shouting over a crate of plating: "Half price, or I take it!" Selena sits on the crate's lid with a lollipop in her cheek and tells him it is not half price. He swings twice. The first fist misses her ear, the second hits the post. Selena is never where the fists land.

He pins a hand beside her head and grins that she has nowhere left to lean. She tells him that if he gets too smug, he will get tripped up. He lunges, her heel pulls the tarp rope taut, his boot catches it, and he goes down in the mud. He stamps off toward the gate, swearing. Only then does Vexana, waiting in the dark, step into the lamplight.
boy-in-the-second-row--change: At the end of the year, in Chang'e's classroom, a boy in the second row keeps asking what her words mean. When she gives the oldest records' rule, that a planet that holds Balance sends the Enders against a people grown too strong, he asks, "Balance?" She tells him: everything kept in check, nothing allowed to grow too big.

When she says the Enders' Control Core must be destroyed, he asks, "Their what?" Whatever steers them all, she says. When she mentions a paper on black holes, he asks, "A what?" She tells him it is a place in space so heavy it swallows whatever comes too near, and that nothing seen falling in has ever come back out, not even light.
boy-under-the-shutter--selena: Before Selrick Academy opens, Selena roams the city on storm nights with the purple spread over her arms and legs. One night after a raid she hears crying under the rain. A shop front has come down, and a small boy lies in the street with its iron shutter across his leg. Two streets off, the rescue lamps are moving away. She calls the purple back under her skin and climbs down.

The shutter feels light under her hand, light enough to press down instead. She lifts it, though two grown men could not have shifted it, and whispers, "Shh. It won't hurt anymore." She stands him up and turns him toward the lamps: "That way. Shout." He limps off shouting, and the lamps turn toward him. Three roofs later she is still asking herself why, and decides it was nothing.
change--layla: When Ruby and Angela ask refuge, one of Chang'e's four conditions is that they sit in the third-year class, beside the two who vouched for them. "Beside us?" says Layla. "You vouched," says Chang'e.

Later Chang'e comes out of a side door of the Academy hall, where Layla is scrubbing the floor in detention, and grins at them all with her whole face: "Great job, guys!" Layla's eyes go to the new coil on Lesley's rifle behind her. Science Division work, she thinks, and she wants it in pieces on her desk.

At the end of that year Layla sits at the front of Chang'e's class, alone. Asked who sends the Enders, she says nobody knows. Then she asks the hard questions first: endanger who, how anyone knows something steers the Enders, and how to get to the void. To the last, Chang'e has to say she does not know yet.
change--small-girl-at-the-shelter: Years after the base fell, its alarm goes again, and Chang'e goes out with her crescents. At the foot of the avenue a pair of iron doors stands open in the seawall: a shelter. A man runs past her with a small girl on his hip, and a woman beside them holds the girl's hand. The girl has her eyes shut. Chang'e counts their steps without meaning to. At ten they are through the doors.

The warden shouts at her to get in. Chang'e says she will definitely protect everyone, and takes her place in front of the doors. Behind her they bang shut, and the bar drops. She holds them even after her ring breaks, until Lesley comes. When the giant falls across the top of the avenue, nobody is under it. Everyone from those streets is behind the iron doors.
fanny--small-boy: When Obsidia's field puts out every suit in the Academy district, a small boy is crying in a shelter doorway up the bay road cut. Fanny gets to her feet, sets them the way soldiers taught her, and raises two blades of plain steel. She builds a wall across the cut and holds it.

The boy comes down the street looking for someone and finds the wall instead. He stands behind Layla with his fists against his eyes and takes hold of her uniform. Fanny kneels beside him and speaks low and soft, nothing like her command voice: "Don't be scared kiddo, everything's gonna be alright."

He asks Layla whether Fanny is her friend. Layla says, "She's my teammate," and Fanny looks down at the stones with her ears gone red. Then a soldier with his arm in a sling walks the boy back up the street.
fanny--third-year-teacher: One morning Fanny lands on Layla's back as she crosses the school roof, late for class. Flying is banned on school grounds, but Fanny has allowed herself a little. The two race down the white spiral stairwell, their feet cross on the last turn, and they roll out into the corridor in a heap.

The classroom door stands open. Their teacher waits with folded arms, and every head turns. It is Fanny's first detention, and she asks the teacher what to bring. Detention turns out to be cleaning the Academy hall.
fanny--vexana: When Vexana comes back in an Ender's robe on the platform by the seawall, Fanny comes over the rail first and keeps her blades up on her. When everyone cries that the Aspirants always stand united, Fanny says it too, her blades still raised. Guinevere later tells her she held on to that in there.

After Vexana and Guinevere strike the Mother Matrix and come back out, Vexana wakes three giants, and Fanny's blades come up at once. "They're mine," says Vexana. "They answer to me." Lesley puts her on the line beside Guinevere. Fanny lets her points drop, but keeps the blades in her hands: an order puts Vexana on the line, not at her back. Not yet.

In the Academy district an Ender steps out behind Vexana, on her left, where she is not looking. For one beat Fanny's blades do not move. Then, telling herself to cover her as she would a squad, she drops between them and strikes the open chest. Vexana looks back and nods once. Fanny turns to the next Ender and leaves her back to Vexana.
guinevere--lesley: Guinevere and Vexana hold the giants' front beside Lesley's squads the day the black ships land. At the end of the year Lesley pins the Academy's first Aspirant Duo badges on the pair. "Undefeated," she says, and that is the whole speech. At the edge of the stage she smiles, small, and it stays.

When Vexana is taken through a door in the corridor, Lesley comes at a run and turns Guinevere away from the wall she is punching. "There's no time to lament." She hands her a notebook to write down everything she saw, reads every line and folds the pages into her coat. By evening she pins VEXANA: MISSING to the board.

Weeks later a records clerk says the form now reads Killed in action. Lesley tells him there is no body, so no finding, and the file stays Missing. Guinevere asks for a squad to lead. Lesley will give her one for a lead. The star is lit, says Guinevere. "That's a light," says Lesley. "Not a lead." Her eye stays on Guinevere a moment, and then she shuts her office door.
guinevere--manners-tutor: At House Baroque, tutors come to teach the young heiress accounts, contracts and manners. The manners tutor talks all day about "a lady's refinement," by which she means how you hold your back. Guinevere glues the tutor's words to Hester's count of three. The next time she falls, on the terrace steps, she is up before Hester reaches her.

Years later, on a fish-market roof, Guinevere gets back to her feet and calls her fall a lady's refinement. And when Ruby plants her scythe on the dirt by the dome's foot and bows, Guinevere knows that bow at once. A manners tutor had spent years on hers.
guinevere--medic: On the fish-market raid Guinevere's wings go out around the thirtieth minute, and Vexana catches her by the wrist at a roof's edge. When the last Ender lies among the fish, a medic takes that wrist to tape it.

While the medic is still taping, Vexana goes back through the portal ahead of the others with Guinevere's lost drone. That night Guinevere lies in bed with her wrist taped. It throbs where Vexana's hand closed on it.
guinevere--will-of-the-planet: In Chang'e's class at the end of the year, Guinevere hears that the Academy thinks a mind sends the Enders: the Will of the Planet, maybe the planet's own, with a body the readings call the Mother Matrix. "Whose mind?" she asks before she can stop herself. She thinks of the claw that raked her arm at the dome's foot. Somebody sent that. When Chang'e names the Control Core, she sits up: something to hit.

That day on the lawn, her head in Vexana's lap, she sits bolt upright and punches at the sky. She will definitely find a way to destroy it. Some Will in the dark sends claws at them and thinks it gets to decide what happens next, she says, and it does not. "We will decide the fate of the world ourselves." Vexana does not answer.
layla--small-boy: When Obsidia's field kills Layla's cannon, she comes down off her roof to the bay road cut. Up the cut, in a shelter doorway, a small boy is crying. Layla holds the wall across the cut with Fanny, counting each Ender's strike aloud.

The boy comes down the street looking for someone and finds the wall instead. He stands behind her with his fists against his eyes. Layla does not turn from the wall. "If you're scared, you can hide behind me." She once said it as a joke. Not now. He takes a fistful of the back of her uniform and holds on.

Fanny kneels and comforts him. He asks Layla whether Fanny is her friend. Layla looks at Fanny and says, "She's my teammate." A soldier with his arm in a sling walks the boy back up the street. Later Ruby makes herself hear his crying, to keep hold of herself.
layla--third-year-teacher: One morning Layla runs along the school roof, bent low, four minutes late for class, sure that nobody checks the roof. Fanny lands on her back, and the two race down the white spiral stairwell until their feet cross and they roll into the corridor in a heap.

The classroom door stands open. The teacher waits with folded arms, and every head turns. "They're really going to throw the book at us this time," says Layla. Then she hears herself add that at least they will be in detention together. Detention is cleaning the Academy hall.
layla--vexana: Layla and Vexana have shared classes for two years, and neither has ever spoken first. In the breach in the northeast sector, Layla sees Guinevere and Vexana hold the other end, Vexana's magic striking whatever reaches for Guinevere's back. Everyone knows them. Their undefeated record is on the courtyard billboard. Layla's is on a rankings board, in second place.

At the gate portal before the fish-market raid, Guinevere introduces herself, and Vexana gives her own name, in case it was needed. Layla keeps score: two years of nothing, and now that she has a team, Vexana talks. She went first. One to her.

Professor Joe sends the Layla-Fanny Team to the west end of the market and the other pair to the east. Weeks later, when Ruby and Angela become Aspirants, Layla turns round in the hall and sees Guinevere waving her whole arm at Vexana by the door.
lesley--officer-with-gray-in-his-beard: The night the base falls, Lesley comes back to find the city's edge burning. On the Shield's channel the squads call for a commander, and nobody answers. On a roof she finds a Shield officer with gray in his beard and a rank armband, shouting into his radio handset while nobody on the channel listens to him. He looks at her face. "You're Lesley," he says. "The rail yard."
He holds out the handset. She says her name into it, and the channel goes quiet. Then the squads answer her, and they hold the avenues, barely.
Between shots she sees a giant walking toward the water, toward the base. "No! It's a decoy!" She shoves the handset back into his hands, tells him to hold there, and runs.
